anat-pr-gland.intro: Start with the gland itself: its zones (where cancer starts), its neighbors (the organs at risk in every plan), and its levels from base to apex. Explore each drawing, then switch to Quiz mode. You will see the same structures on MRI and CT in the Imaging section.

plates.title: The Zones (McNeal)
plates.caption: 3D drawing of the prostate cut open to show its zones, with the seminal vesicles behind it. Posterior is toward the upper left, anterior toward the lower right. Häggström M, Prostate zones (Wikimedia Commons), CC0; labels removed.

hotspots.label: Peripheral Zone (PZ)
hotspots.blurb: The posterior and lateral gland (green), right against the rectum. About 70% of the glandular tissue and about 70% of cancers, which is why a DRE can feel them.

hotspots.label: Central Zone (CZ)
hotspots.blurb: A cone around the ejaculatory ducts at the base (teal). Few cancers start here, but they tend to be aggressive, and it sits next to the seminal vesicles.

hotspots.label: Transition Zone (TZ)
hotspots.blurb: Wraps around the urethra (yellow). Where BPH grows as men age, and where about 20% of cancers start.

hotspots.label: Anterior Fibromuscular Stroma
hotspots.blurb: The front of the gland (orange). Muscle, not glands, so cancer rarely starts here, but anterior tumors are missed by a DRE.

hotspots.label: Prostatic Urethra
hotspots.blurb: Runs straight through the gland from the bladder neck to the apex. Urethral dose drives urinary side effects.

hotspots.label: Ejaculatory Duct
hotspots.blurb: Formed where the vas and seminal vesicle join; runs through the central zone to the urethra.

hotspots.label: Seminal Vesicles
hotspots.blurb: Paired glands behind the bladder, attached at the base. Tumor growing into them is a high-risk feature.

hotspots.label: Vas Deferens (Ampulla)
hotspots.blurb: Joins the seminal vesicle duct to form the ejaculatory duct.

hotspots.label: Membranous Urethra
hotspots.blurb: Leaves the apex and passes through the external sphincter.

plates.title: Sagittal View: Neighbors
plates.caption: Midline side view of the male pelvis, anterior on the left. The prostate sits under the bladder, in front of the rectum. Cancer Research UK diagram 358 (Wikimedia Commons), CC BY-SA 4.0; labels removed.

hotspots.label: Prostate
hotspots.blurb: About the size of a walnut, wrapped around the urethra just below the bladder.

hotspots.label: Bladder
hotspots.blurb: Sits on top of the prostate base. Treated comfortably full to push bowel out of the field and spread bladder dose.

hotspots.label: Bladder Neck
hotspots.blurb: Where the bladder empties into the prostatic urethra, at the base of the gland.

hotspots.label: Seminal Vesicles
hotspots.blurb: Behind the bladder and above the prostate. Proximal seminal vesicles are often included in the target.

hotspots.label: Denonvilliers' Fascia
hotspots.blurb: The thin layer between the prostate and the rectum. A hydrogel spacer is injected just behind it to push the rectum away.

hotspots.label: Rectum
hotspots.blurb: Directly behind the prostate. The organ that limits dose: proctitis and bleeding. It is also why a DRE can feel the gland.

hotspots.label: Membranous Urethra / Sphincter
hotspots.blurb: Just below the apex. The external sphincter here controls continence; the penile bulb sits just below it.

hotspots.label: Vas Deferens
hotspots.blurb: Runs up from the testis, over the bladder, and down to join the seminal vesicle behind it.

hotspots.label: Ureter
hotspots.blurb: Enters the back of the bladder near the seminal vesicles.

plates.title: Base, Mid-Gland, Apex
plates.caption: Close-up of the same sagittal drawing: the gland from the base under the bladder down to the apex. Cancer Research UK diagram 358 (Wikimedia Commons), CC BY-SA 4.0; labels removed.

hotspots.label: Base
hotspots.blurb: The top of the gland, pressed against the bladder neck. The seminal vesicles attach here, so tumor at the base is the route into them.

hotspots.label: Mid-Gland
hotspots.blurb: The bulk of the gland and most of the peripheral zone. Biopsies sample the base, mid-gland, and apex on each side.

hotspots.label: Apex
hotspots.blurb: The narrow bottom tip, just above the sphincter. Hard to see on CT, and the most common place for a positive surgical margin.

hotspots.label: Bladder Neck
hotspots.blurb: The outlet of the bladder, sitting on the base.

hotspots.label: Prostatic Urethra
hotspots.blurb: Runs from the bladder neck down through the gland to the apex.

hotspots.label: Ejaculatory Duct
hotspots.blurb: Enters from the seminal vesicles at the back of the base and angles down to the urethra.

hotspots.label: Seminal Vesicle
hotspots.blurb: Behind the bladder, attached to the base.

hotspots.label: Membranous Urethra
hotspots.blurb: Below the apex, through the external sphincter.

hotspots.label: Rectum
hotspots.blurb: Behind the whole length of the gland, closest at the mid-gland and apex.

anat-pr-nodes.intro: Prostate lymph drains in a predictable order: obturator and internal iliac → external iliac and presacral → common iliac → para-aortic. Learn the chains on the map; you will find the same nodes on CT in the Imaging section.

plates.title: Pelvic Nodal Map (Frontal)
plates.caption: Pelvic and para-aortic lymph nodes (green) along the aorta, IVC, and iliac vessels. Obturator and presacral nodes are shown on axial CT in the Imaging section. Cancer Research UK diagram (Wikimedia Commons), CC BY-SA 4.0; labels removed.

hotspots.label: Para-aortic Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Along the aorta and IVC. M1a. Not in standard elective fields.

hotspots.label: Common Iliac Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Above the iliac bifurcation. M1a by AJCC, but the distal common iliac (up to L5/S1) is covered in elective pelvic RT.

hotspots.label: External Iliac Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Along the external iliac vessels at the pelvic brim. N1.

hotspots.label: Internal Iliac (Hypogastric) Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Along the internal iliac vessels, deep in the pelvis. First echelon. N1.

hotspots.label: Inguinal Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Groin. M1a for prostate cancer (they drain the skin, anus, and vulva/penis).

hotspots.label: Prostate
hotspots.blurb: The primary. Periprostatic nodes drain laterally to the obturator and internal iliac groups.

hotspots.label: Bladder
hotspots.blurb: Sits in front of the prostate. The pelvic nodal chains run along the vessels on either side of it.
